cs0168.title: CS0168
cs0168.short: A declared variable is never used.
cs0168.summary: This warning appears when a local variable is declared but its value is never read. If a value is assigned but still never used, see [[cs0219|CS0219]].
cs0168.why: An unused variable may indicate leftover code or an implementation step that was forgotten.
cs0168.tips: Remove it if it is not needed; keeping variables only because they might be useful later usually makes code harder to read.

badNotes.1: unused is declared but never used

cs0219.title: CS0219
cs0219.short: A variable receives a value but is never used.
cs0219.summary: This appears when a value is assigned to a variable but that value is never read afterward. If the variable is only declared and never used, see [[cs0168|CS0168]].
cs0219.why: Because the computed value has no effect on the result, the assignment may be leftover or indicate missing logic.
cs0219.tips: This warning often remains after temporary debugging code has been removed.

badNotes.1: answer is assigned but never used

goodNotes.2: Use the value that was computed

cs0618.title: CS0618
cs0618.short: Code is using an API marked Obsolete.
cs0618.summary: The referenced type or member is still available, but its provider has marked it as obsolete or deprecated.
cs0618.why: The API author wants callers to migrate to a newer replacement or pattern.
cs0618.tips: If the warning message names a replacement API, follow that guidance. If a member cannot be found after migration, also check [[cs1061|CS1061]].

cs1998.title: CS1998
cs1998.short: An async method contains no await.
cs1998.summary: This warning appears when a method using [[async-await|async / await]] does not actually await asynchronous work and therefore runs synchronously.
cs1998.why: Without await, there is usually little reason to build the async state machine.
cs1998.tips: If no asynchronous work is needed, remove async and consider returning [[task|Task]].FromResult instead.

badNotes.1: The method is async but contains no await

cs4014.title: CS4014
cs4014.short: A Task is started without being awaited.
cs4014.summary: The returned [[task|Task]] from an asynchronous method is not [[async-await|awaited]], so completion and exceptions may be missed.
cs4014.why: Without await, execution can continue to the next line before SaveAsync has completed.
cs4014.tips: Even when intentionally not waiting, decide how failures will be observed. Changing code to async void just to avoid awaiting creates a different problem.

badNotes.1: Execution continues without waiting for this Task

goodNotes.1: Await the Task so completion is observed

cs8600.title: CS8600
cs8600.short: A possibly null value is assigned to a non-nullable reference type.
cs8600.summary: [[nullable|Nullable reference type]] analysis has determined that the assigned value may be null.
cs8600.why: string declares a non-null value, while maybeName has type string?.
cs8600.tips: Instead of silencing the warning with !, decide what should happen when the value is null, for example with the ?? operator.

badNotes.2: A value that may be null is assigned to string

goodNotes.2: Provide a value for the null case

cs8618.title: CS8618
cs8618.short: A non-nullable field or property is not initialized.
cs8618.summary: With [[nullable|nullable reference types]] enabled, this appears when a member that should not be null may still be null when construction finishes.
cs8618.why: Immediately after constructing User, Name could still be null.
cs8618.tips: Consider requiring the value in the constructor or using a required [[properties|property]].

badNotes.3: Non-nullable Name has not been initialized

goodNotes.3: Give Name a non-null value at construction time

cs8625.title: CS8625
cs8625.short: null is assigned to a non-nullable reference type.
cs8625.summary: With [[nullable|nullable reference types]] enabled, this appears when null is passed or assigned where null is not allowed.
cs8625.why: The declaration says string cannot be null, but the assignment supplies null.
cs8625.tips: If null is a valid state, use ?. When a possibly null value is assigned to a non-nullable reference, also check [[cs8600|CS8600]].

badNotes.1: null is assigned to a non-nullable string

goodNotes.1: Use string? when null is allowed

cs0108.title: CS0108: Unintentionally hiding an inherited member
cs0108.short: A derived declaration has the same name as an inherited member without stating its intent.
cs0108.summary: CS0108 warns about member hiding. Hiding selects by the variable's compile-time type, unlike overriding a virtual member, which participates in runtime dispatch.
cs0108.why: ReportPrinter.Print is a new member because BasePrinter.Print is not virtual. A BasePrinter reference still calls the base member even when it refers to a ReportPrinter.
cs0108.tips: Use new to acknowledge deliberate hiding, as shown, or change the base member to virtual and use override when [[inheritance-polymorphism|polymorphic dispatch]] is the intended design.

badNotes.8: This declaration hides the inherited Print without stating that intent

goodNotes.8: new explicitly selects member hiding rather than overriding
